'''乾'''（けん）は[[八卦]]の一つ。卦の形は[[画像:Ken.png]]であり、三爻がすべて陽。または[[六十四卦]]の一つであり、乾為天。乾上乾下で構成される。
== 八卦 == 天・健・馬・首・父・君などを象徴する。
[[Category:易|けん]]

revision.text:
{{otheruses|Nine Stars of Divination|Nine Stars in Indian Astronomy|Nine Luminaries}} {{Cite source|date=December 2018}} {{color}} '''Nine Stars''' ({{ill|Nine Stars|ja|九星}}, Kyūsei) is a form of [[folk belief]] originating from ancient [[China]], consisting of nine stars: '''First White''', '''Second Black''', '''Third Blue''', '''Fourth Green''', '''Fifth Yellow''', '''Sixth White''', '''Seventh Red''', '''Eighth White''', and '''Ninth Purple'''.
The term "Nine Stars" can refer to several systems, and the one described here is specifically referred to as the "Purple White Nine Stars" or "Seven Colored Stars."
== Origin == The Nine Stars system originates from the following {{ill|magic square|ja|魔方陣}}:
{| class="wikitable" |- |Four||Nine||Two |- |Three||Five||Seven |- |Eight||One||Six |}
In this magic square, the sum of any row, column, or diagonal equals 15. It uses the numbers 1 through 9 exactly once in a 3×3 grid. This configuration, called the '''Later Heaven Arrangement''' ({{ill|Later Heaven Arrangement|ja|後天定位盤}}), is the only one of its kind, excluding rotations and reflections. These numbers are paired with seven colors (white, black, blue, green, yellow, red, and purple), the {{ill|five elements|ja|五行思想}} ({{ill|wood|ja|木}}, {{ill|fire|ja|火}}, {{ill|earth|ja|土}}, {{ill|metal|ja|金}}, and {{ill|water|ja|水}}), the {{ill|ten heavenly stems|ja|十干}}, the {{ill|twelve earthly branches|ja|十二支}}, and the {{ill|eight trigrams|ja|八卦}} of {{ill|I Ching|ja|易経}}. When these numbers shift positions, interpretations are added to form the "Nine Stars."
According to legend, {{ill|Yu the Great|ja|禹}}, founder of the {{ill|Xia Dynasty|ja|夏王朝}}, conceived this magic square when he encountered a sacred turtle emerging from the {{ill|Luo River|ja|洛水}}. This magic square is called the "Writing of the Luo" ({{ill|Luo Writing|ja|洛書}}), one of the {{ill|River Chart and Luo Writing|ja|河図洛書}}.
== The Nine Stars == In Japanese {{ill|Onmyōdō|ja|陰陽道}}, the following table associates the Nine Stars with the {{ill|five elements|ja|五行思想}}, {{ill|directions|ja|方位}}, {{ill|eight trigrams|ja|八卦}}, and colors, forming the '''Nine Stars Chart''' used to predict {{ill|fortune|ja|運勢}} and the {{ill|auspiciousness|ja|吉凶}} of directions based on a person's birth year.
{| class="wikitable" |- ! Star ! Reading ! Five Element ! Direction ! Eight Trigram ! {{otheruses|Nine Stars of Divination|Nine Stars in Indian Astronomy|Nine Luminaries}} {{Cite source|date=December 2018}} {| class="wikitable" |- | {{ill|Qian|ja|乾}} |- | {{ill|Dui|ja|兌}} |- | {{ill|Gen|ja|艮}} |- | {{ill|Li|ja|離}} |}{{color}} '''Nine Stars''' ({{ill|Nine Stars|ja|九星}}, Kyūsei) is a form of [[folk belief]] originating from ancient [[China]], consisting of nine stars: '''First White''', '''Second Black''', '''Third Blue''', '''Fourth Green''', '''Fifth Yellow''', '''Sixth White''', '''Seventh Red''', '''Eighth White''', and '''Ninth Purple'''.
The term "Nine Stars" can refer to several systems, and the one described here is specifically referred to as the "Purple White Nine Stars" or "Seven Colored Stars."
== Origin == The Nine Stars system originates from the following {{ill|magic square|ja|魔方陣}}:
{| class="wikitable" |- |Four||Nine||Two |- |Three||Five||Seven |- |Eight||One||Six |}
In this magic square, the sum of any row, column, or diagonal equals 15. It uses the numbers 1 through 9 exactly once in a 3×3 grid. This configuration, called the '''Later Heaven Arrangement''' ({{ill|Later Heaven Arrangement|ja|後天定位盤}}), is the only one of its kind, excluding rotations and reflections. These numbers are paired with seven colors (white, black, blue, green, yellow, red, and purple), the {{ill|five elements|ja|五行思想}} ({{ill|wood|ja|木}}, {{ill|fire|ja|火}}, {{ill|earth|ja|土}}, {{ill|metal|ja|金}}, and {{ill|water|ja|水}}), the {{ill|ten heavenly stems|ja|十干}}, the {{ill|twelve earthly branches|ja|十二支}}, and the {{ill|eight trigrams|ja|八卦}} of {{ill|I Ching|ja|易経}}. When these numbers shift positions, interpretations are added to form the "Nine Stars."
According to legend, {{ill|Yu the Great|ja|禹}}, founder of the {{ill|Xia Dynasty|ja|夏王朝}}, conceived this magic square when he encountered a sacred turtle emerging from the {{ill|Luo River|ja|洛水}}. This magic square is called the "Writing of the Luo" ({{ill|Luo Writing|ja|洛書}}), one of the {{ill|River Chart and Luo Writing|ja|河図洛書}}.

According to legend, {{ill|Yu the Great|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:禹]], founder of the {{ill|Xia Dynasty|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:夏王朝]], conceived this magic square when he encountered a sacred turtle emerging from the {{ill|Luo River|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:洛水]]. This magic square is called the "Writing of the Luo" ({{ill|Luo Writing|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:洛書]]), one of the {{ill|River Chart and Luo Writing|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:河図洛書]].
== The Nine Stars == In Japanese {{ill|Onmyōdō|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:陰陽道]], the following table associates the Nine Stars with the {{ill|five elements|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:五行思想]], {{ill|directions|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:方位]], {{ill|eight trigrams|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:八卦]], and colors, forming the '''Nine Stars Chart''' used to predict {{ill|fortune|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:運勢]] and the {{ill|auspiciousness|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:吉凶]] of directions based on a person's birth year.
{| class="wikitable" |- ! Star ! Reading ! Five Element ! Direction ! Eight Trigram ! Color |- ! {{ill|First White Water Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:一白水星]] | Ippaku Suisei | Water | {{ill|North|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:北]] | {{ill|Kan|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:坎]] | style="background:white;"| White |- ! {{ill|Second Black Earth Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:二黒土星]] | Jikoku Dosei | Earth | Southwest | {{ill|Kun|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:坤]] | style="background:black;color:white;"| Black |- ! {{ill|Third Blue Wood Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:三碧木星]] | Sanpeki Mokusei | Wood | {{ill|East|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:東]] | {{ill|Zhen|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:震]] | style="background:blue;color:white;"| Blue |- ! {{ill|Fourth Green Wood Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:四緑木星]] | Shiroku Mokusei | Wood | Southeast | {{ill|Xun|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:巽]] | style="background:green;color:white;"| Green |- ! {{ill|Fifth Yellow Earth Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:五黄土星]] | Goō Dosei | Earth | Center | {{ill|Tai Chi|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:太極]] | style="background:yellow;"| Yellow |- ! {{ill|Sixth White Metal Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:六白金星]] | Roppaku Kinsei | Metal | Northwest | | style="background:white;"| White |- ! {{ill|Seventh Red Metal Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:七赤金星]] | Shichiseki Kinsei | Metal | {{ill|West|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:西]] | | style="background:red;color:white;"| Red |- ! {{ill|Eighth White Earth Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:八白土星]] | Happaku Dosei | Earth | Northeast | | style="background:white;"| White |- ! {{ill|Ninth Purple Fire Star|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:九紫火星]] | Kyūshi Kasei | Fire | {{ill|South|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:南]] | | style="background:purple;color:white;"| Purple |}
Despite their names, the Nine Stars are not related to celestial objects like the planets in the {{ill|Solar System|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:太陽系]].
== Relationships Among the Stars == The relationships among the Nine Stars follow the {{ill|five elements theory|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:五行思想]]:

Sixth White Metal Star | First White Water Star, Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star | Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star |- ! Seventh Red Metal Star | First White Water Star, Second Black Earth Star, Fifth Yellow Earth Star, Eighth White Earth Star | Sixth White Metal Star, Seventh Red Metal Star | Third Blue Wood Star, Fourth Green Wood Star, Ninth Purple Fire Star |- ! These relationships are used for predicting {{ill|compatibility|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:相性]], {{ill|fortune|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:運勢]], and {{ill|auspicious directions|en}}[[category:new pages]][[ja:吉方位]].

{{Otheruses}} {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}} '''Ken''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wu Xing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan (☵)|ja|坎}}, {{ill|Gen (☶)|ja|艮}}, {{ill|Zhen (☳)|ja|震}}, {{ill|Xun (☴)|ja|巽}}, {{ill|Li (☲)|ja|離}}, {{ill|Kun (☷)|ja|坤}}, {{ill|Dui (☱)|ja|兌}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{Bagua}} '''Ken''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan (☵)|ja|坎}}, {{ill|Gen (☶)|ja|艮}}, {{ill|Zhen (☳)|ja|震}}, {{ill|Xun (☴)|ja|巽}}, {{ill|Li (☲)|ja|離}}, {{ill|Kun (☷)|ja|坤}}, {{ill|Dui (☱)|ja|兌}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{Bagua}} '''Ken''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{Bagua}} '''Ken''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{Bagua}} '''Ken''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Ken below and Ken above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Ken symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Ken is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Ken corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Ken (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.

When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Ken is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Ken is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.

Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. {{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
[[Category:I Ching]] [[ja:乾]]

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位}}, Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)|12=draft|12=draft}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)|12=draft|12=draft}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)|12=draft|12=draft}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|12=draft|12=draft}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南|12=draft|12=draft}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses|Qian}} {{Bagua}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the {{ill|Bagua|ja|八卦|12=draft|12=draft}}. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻|12=draft|12=draft}}. It is also one of the {{ill|Sixty-Four Hexagrams|ja|六十四卦|12=draft|12=draft}}, known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qian (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天|12=draft|12=draft}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|12=draft|12=draft}}, it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|12=draft|12=draft}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲|12=draft|12=draft}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Wood element in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|lt=Wuxing|ja|五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}, and the {{ill|east|ja|東|12=draft|12=draft}} among the {{ill|Five Directions|ja|五方|12=draft|12=draft}}. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)|12=draft|12=draft}}, the Water element, and the {{ill|north|ja|北|12=draft|12=draft}}. The Earthly Branches {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)|12=draft|12=draft}} are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a {{ill|cardinal direction|ja|方位|12=draft|12=draft}}, Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|12=draft|12=draft}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the {{ill|Earthly Branches|ja|十二支|12=draft|12=draft}}, intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kan (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gen (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhen (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xun (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (☴)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Li|ja|離|1=Li (Bagua)|lt=Li|lt=Li (☲)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Kun|ja|坤|1=Kun (Bagua)|lt=Kun|lt=Kun (☷)|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Dui (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)|12=draft|12=draft}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between {{ill|Xu (戌)|ja|戌|1=Dog (zodiac)|lt=Dog (戌)|12=draft|12=draft}} (*inu*) and {{ill|Hai (亥)|ja|亥|1=Pig (zodiac)|lt=Pig (亥)|12=draft|12=draft}} (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|12=draft|12=draft}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing {{ill|south|ja|南|12=draft|12=draft}}. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{Otheruses}} {{八卦}} '''乾'''（けん）は[[八卦]]の一つ。卦の形は{{resize|125%|'''☰'''}}であり、三[[爻]]がすべて陽。または[[六十四卦]]の一つであり、[[周易上経三十卦の一覧#乾|乾為天]]。乾下乾上で構成される。
== 卦象 == 天・健・馬・首・父・君などを象徴する。[[方位]]としては[[北西]]を示す。
[[納甲]]では[[甲]]、[[五行思想|五行]]の[[木]]、[[五方]]の[[東]]、または[[壬]]、[[五行思想|五行]]の[[水]]、[[五方]]の[[北]]に当てられる。戌と亥は、泣く、嬉しい、喜び、友達など。
== 方角 == [[方位|方角]]としては[[北西]]の方角になる。全方位（東西南北）を十二支で12等分した場合、北東、東南、南西、西北が表現できないため、これと別に北から時計回りに坎（かん）、艮（ごん）、震（しん）、巽（そん）、離（り）、坤（こん）、兌（だ）、乾（けん）の八卦を使って方角を表現した<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」国立国会図書館 2021年12月16日閲覧</ref>。[[戌]]（いぬ）と[[亥]]（い）の間であることから乾は「いぬい」とも読まれる。
== 先天図 == 伏羲先天八卦における次序は一であり、方位は四正卦の一つで[[南]]に配される。陰陽消息は陽が極まったところである。
== 脚注 == {{Reflist}}

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q2384853]] Wikidata name: trigram Qian [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:54, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Otheruses|Qian|qq=}} {{Bagua|qq=}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the [[:en:Bagua|Bagua]]. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''|qq=}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=}}. It is also one of the [[:en:Hexagram (I Ching)|Sixty-Four Hexagrams]], known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qián (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qián (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian as Heaven|13=User:Immanuelle/Qián (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian as Heaven|13=User:Immanuelle/Qián (Bagua)|qq=}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five directions]], it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)|lt=Kinoe (甲)|2=ja|3=甲|4=zh|5=甲|1=Kinoe (甲)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jia (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoe (甲)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jia (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoe (甲)|qq=}}, the Wood element in [[:en:Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|Five Elements (Wuxing)]], and the [[:en:East|east]] among the [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five Directions]]. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)|lt=Mizunoe (壬)|2=ja|3=壬|4=zh|5=壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ren (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoe (壬)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ren (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoe (壬)|qq=}}, the Water element, and the [[:en:North|north]]. The Earthly Branches [[:en:Dog (zodiac)|Dog (戌)]] and [[:en:Pig (zodiac)|Pig (亥)]] are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five directions]], Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the [[:en:Earthly Branches|Earthly Branches]], intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kǎn (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坎|lt=Kǎn (坎)|1=Kǎn (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kǎn (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kǎn (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gèn (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gèn (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gèn (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gèn (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhèn (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between [[:en:Dog (zodiac)|Dog (戌)]] (*inu*) and [[:en:Pig (zodiac)|Pig (亥)]] (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing [[:en:South|south]]. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q2384853]] Wikidata name: trigram Qian [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:54, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Otheruses|Qian|qq=}} {{Bagua|qq=}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the [[:en:Bagua|Bagua]]. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''|qq=}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=}}. It is also one of the [[:en:Hexagram (I Ching)|Sixty-Four Hexagrams]], known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qián (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qián (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian as Heaven|13=User:Immanuelle/Qián (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian as Heaven|13=User:Immanuelle/Qián (Bagua)|qq=}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five directions]], it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)|lt=Kinoe (甲)|2=ja|3=甲|4=zh|5=甲|1=Kinoe (甲)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jia (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoe (甲)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jia (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoe (甲)|qq=}}, the Wood element in [[:en:Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|Five Elements (Wuxing)]], and the [[:en:East|east]] among the [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five Directions]]. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)|lt=Mizunoe (壬)|2=ja|3=壬|4=zh|5=壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ren (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoe (壬)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ren (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoe (壬)|qq=}}, the Water element, and the [[:en:North|north]]. The Earthly Branches [[:en:Dog (zodiac)|Dog (戌)]] and [[:en:Pig (zodiac)|Pig (亥)]] are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five directions]], Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the [[:en:Earthly Branches|Earthly Branches]], intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kǎn (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坎|lt=Kǎn (坎)|1=Kǎn (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kǎn and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between [[:en:Dog (zodiac)|Dog (戌)]] (*inu*) and [[:en:Pig (zodiac)|Pig (亥)]] (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing [[:en:South|south]]. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.

{{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q2384853]] Wikidata name: trigram Qian [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:54, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Otheruses|Qian|qq=}} {{Bagua|qq=}} '''Qian''' (乾) is one of the [[:en:Bagua|Bagua]]. Its trigram form is {{resize|125%|'''☰'''|qq=}} and consists of three Yang (⚊) {{ill|Yao (lines)|ja|爻|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yao (lines)|qq=}}. It is also one of the [[:en:Hexagram (I Ching)|Sixty-Four Hexagrams]], known as {{ill|Qian as Heaven|ja|乾|1=Qián (Bagua)|2=ja|3=乾|lt=Qian (乾)|1=Qián (Bagua)|lt=Qian為天|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian as Heaven|13=User:Immanuelle/Qián (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Qian as Heaven|13=User:Immanuelle/Qián (Bagua)|qq=}}, consisting of Qian below and Qian above.
== Trigram Symbolism == Qian symbolizes heaven, strength, horses, the head, the father, and the sovereign. As a [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five directions]], it represents the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}.
In the {{ill|Na Jia|ja|納甲|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Na Jia|qq=}} system, Qian is associated with {{ill|Jia (Heavenly Stem)|ja|甲|1=Kinoe (甲)|lt=Kinoe (甲)|2=ja|3=甲|4=zh|5=甲|1=Kinoe (甲)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jia (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoe (甲)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jia (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinoe (甲)|qq=}}, the Wood element in [[:en:Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|Five Elements (Wuxing)]], and the [[:en:East|east]] among the [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five Directions]]. Alternatively, it can also correspond to {{ill|Ren (Heavenly Stem)|ja|壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)|lt=Mizunoe (壬)|2=ja|3=壬|4=zh|5=壬|1=Mizunoe (壬)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ren (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoe (壬)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ren (Heavenly Stem)|13=User:Immanuelle/Mizunoe (壬)|qq=}}, the Water element, and the [[:en:North|north]]. The Earthly Branches [[:en:Dog (zodiac)|Dog (戌)]] and [[:en:Pig (zodiac)|Pig (亥)]] are associated with emotions such as crying, joy, happiness, and friendship.
== Direction == As a [[:en:Cardinal direction|Five directions]], Qian corresponds to the {{ill|northwest|ja|北西|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/northwest|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. When the four cardinal directions (east, west, south, north) are divided into twelve parts using the [[:en:Earthly Branches|Earthly Branches]], intermediate directions such as northeast, southeast, southwest, and northwest cannot be fully expressed. To address this, the eight trigrams—{{ill|Kan|ja|坎|1=Kǎn (Bagua)|2=ja|3=坎|lt=Kǎn (坎)|1=Kǎn (Bagua)|lt=Kan|lt=Kan (☵)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kǎn (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kan|13=User:Immanuelle/Kǎn (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gen|ja|艮|1=Gèn (Bagua)|2=ja|3=艮|lt=Gen (艮)|1=Gèn (Bagua)|lt=Gen|lt=Gen (☶)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gèn (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gen|13=User:Immanuelle/Gèn (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Zhen|ja|震|1=Zhèn (Bagua)|2=ja|3=震|lt=Zhèn (震)|1=Zhèn (Bagua)|lt=Zhen|lt=Zhen (☳)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhèn (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhen|13=User:Immanuelle/Zhèn (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Xun|ja|巽|1=Xùn (Bagua)|2=ja|3=巽|lt=Xun (巽)|1=Xùn (Bagua)|lt=Xun|lt=Xun (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kun|13=User:Immanuelle/Kūn (Bagua)|qq=}}, {{ill|Dui|ja|兌|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|2=ja|3=兌|4=zh-yue|5=兌卦|6=ko|7=태 (괘)|8=fr|9=Duì|10=nl|11=Meer (trigram)|12=pt|13=Duì (I Ching)|14=zh-min-nan|15=Tōe-kòa|lt=Dui (兌)|1=Duì (Bagua)|lt=Dui|lt\=Dui (☱)|lt=Dui (☱)|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dui|13=User:Immanuelle/Duì (Bagua)|qq=}}, and Qian (乾)—are used to indicate directions<ref>「[https://www.ndl.go.jp/koyomi/chapter3/s2.html 干支2方位神]」National Diet Library, accessed December 16, 2021.</ref>. Because it lies between [[:en:Dog (zodiac)|Dog (戌)]] (*inu*) and [[:en:Pig (zodiac)|Pig (亥)]] (*i*), Qian is also read as *Inui* (いぬい).
== Earlier Heaven Arrangement == In the {{ill|Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|ja|伏羲先天八卦|qq=draft|qq=|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fuxi Earlier Heaven Bagua|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Qian is the first in sequence and is positioned as one of the four cardinal trigrams, representing [[:en:South|south]]. In terms of Yin-Yang transformation, it represents the extreme of Yang.
